audit.whatIsWrong: All seven chart rows disagreed across layers. Full phases[].side read Swain/Swain/Skill/Skill/Swain/Skill/Skill; content win[] and the packet levelChart both read Skill/Skill/Swain/Swain/Ekko/Swain/Swain. Separately the packet flags that this chart contradicts the data: Ekko wins 55.45% over 909 games while the chart hands Swain four stages to Ekko's one.
audit.why: The layer alignment is groundable — Nevermove arrives at 3 and is the row that changes the lane, and Demonic Ascension at 6 is answered by Chronobreak arriving the same level. Whether the chart or the win rate is the wrong artifact is not decidable from the kits, so I did not invent a verdict.
audit.corrected: Full sides moved onto the content values with every why rewritten in the same proposal. The chart-versus-win-rate contradiction is escalated rather than guessed at.

audit.whatIsWrong: The spikes described a "E root plus W drain" combo. That interaction does not exist: Swain's W is Vision of Empire, a 5500-to-7500 range demon eye that damages, slows and reveals — the drain is his R, Demonic Ascension. The page invented a level-3 sustain combo out of two unrelated abilities.
audit.why: enemyKit W text: opens a demon eye that deals damage and slows enemies, champions hit are revealed and grant a Soul Fragment. enemyKit R text: transforms into a demon and drains health from nearby enemy champions.
audit.corrected: Spikes and whys now describe what actually spikes at 3 — Nevermove (12s) rooting on the return pass and then pulling you in — and W is described as the map-range eye that farms Soul Fragments off you.
sources: brief enemyKit W, E and R text

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions were absent. Nevermove roots on the RETURN pass, not the outbound one, and Swain can then pull every rooted champion toward him — so the dodge is the second wave, and the danger is being dragged out of your own escape. And Ravenous Flock heals him off Soul Fragments while permanently raising his maximum health, which is what makes chip damage worthless and makes stacked resistances the wrong answer.
audit.why: enemyKit E text: it then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits; Swain can then choose to pull all rooted champions closer; shorter cooldown during Demonic Ascension. enemyKit P flags: heal and percentHealth; text: ravens collect Soul Fragments that heal him and permanently increase his maximum health. Both missingInteractions rules for this matchup are anti-heal and resistances-invalidated.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns, dos, don'ts and trading now state the return-pass root and the pull, that Nevermove's cooldown drops during his ultimate, and that Grievous Wounds rather than raw resistances decides extended trades.

notes: All seven chart rows were split across layers; full moved onto the content values, which match the packet levelChart, with every why rewritten alongside. I did NOT resolve the packet's own flagged contradiction (chart gives Swain 4/7 while Ekko wins 55.45%) — see questions. The biggest correction here is a fabricated interaction that was on the live page: the content layer described an 'E root plus W drain' level-3 combo in three separate fields. Swain's W is Vision of Empire, a 5500-7500 range eye that damages, slows, reveals and grants him a Soul Fragment; the drain is his R. Also newly stated: Nevermove roots on the RETURN pass and is followed by an optional pull, its cooldown shortens during Demonic Ascension, and Ravenous Flock permanently raises his maximum health, which is why Grievous Wounds and not resistances is the answer. Not verified and therefore not written: whether Ekko's W anomaly stun interrupts the Nevermove pull, and whether Chronobreak's untargetable frames break an existing root.
